name: Wheat (गेहूं / கோதுமை / ਕਣਕ / గోధుਮలు)
suitableRegions: Indo-Gangetic Plains, Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, MP, Rajasthan, Bihar
climate: Cool and dry during early vegetative growth, warm and dry during ripening and harvest.
soilTypes: Alluvial, Loamy, Clay Loam (well-drained fertile soils)
waterDesc: 4-6 irrigations at critical stages: CRI (21 DAS), Tillering (40-45 DAS), Jointing (60-65 DAS), Flowering (80-85 DAS), Milk stage (100-105 DAS), Dough stage (115-120 DAS)
sowingWindow: 1 Nov – 25 Nov (Timely Sown), up to 15 Dec (Late Sown)
spacing: 20-22.5 cm row-to-row, 5 cm plant-to-plant; Sowing depth: 4-5 cm

fertilizerPlan.nitrogen: 120 kg N / ha (split into basal + 2 top dressings at 1st & 2nd irrigation)
fertilizerPlan.phosphorus: 60 kg P2O5 / ha (basal application with seed drill)
fertilizerPlan.zinc: 25 kg Zinc Sulphate / ha once in 2 years

nutrientDeficiencies: Yellowing of lower leaves (Nitrogen), purpling of leaf margins (Phosphorus), chlorosis in younger leaves (Zinc).
commonPests: Aphids (Mahun), Armyworm, Termites (at seedling stage), Brown Mite
commonDiseases: Yellow (Stripe) Rust, Brown (Leaf) Rust, Loose Smut, Karnal Bunt, Powdery Mildew
preventionPractices: Seed treatment with Carboxin/Thiram @ 2g/kg seed; spray Propiconazole 25% EC (1 ml/L) on early yellow rust symptoms; avoid excessive nitrogen.
postHarvest: Threshing at 12-14% grain moisture; clean foreign seeds and chaff; air-dry to <12% moisture before storage.
storageGuidance: Store in hermetic metal bins / Pusa bins; treat bins with Malathion 50% EC spray; use neem leaves or aluminium phosphide tablets for weevil prevention.
marketConsiderations: Government Minimum Support Price (MSP) procurement active in April-May; high milling demand in flour mills and biscuits industry.
intercropping: Mustard intercropping (Wheat + Mustard 9:1 or 8:1 row ratio), Gram intercropping.
riskFactors: Terminal heat stress during March grain-filling stage; unseasonal hailstorms during harvesting; waterlogging during early tillering.
tips: Sow certified high-yielding varieties: HD-2967, DBW-187 (Karan Vandana), DBW-303, PBW-725. Ensure 1st irrigation at Crown Root Initiation (CRI) stage exactly 21 days after sowing.

name: Mustard / Sarson (सरसों / கடுகு / ਸਰ੍ਹੋਂ / ఆవాలు)
suitableRegions: Rajasthan, Haryana, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Gujarat, West Bengal
climate: Cool and dry subtropical climate; requires clear sunny days during flowering.
soilTypes: Sandy Loam, Alluvial, Light Loam (well-drained soils)
waterDesc: 2-3 light irrigations: 1st at pre-flowering (30-35 DAS), 2nd at pod development (60-65 DAS). Sensitive to water stagnation.
spacing: 30-45 cm row-to-row, 10-15 cm plant-to-plant; Sowing depth: 2-3 cm

fertilizerPlan.nitrogen: 80 kg N / ha (half basal, half at 1st irrigation)
fertilizerPlan.phosphorus: 40 kg P2O5 / ha (basal with single super phosphate for sulphur content)
fertilizerPlan.sulphur: 20-25 kg elemental Sulphur / ha (crucial for high oil synthesis)

nutrientDeficiencies: Cupped and yellow young leaves with purple undersides (Sulphur deficiency), stunted growth (Nitrogen).
commonPests: Mustard Aphid (Lipaphis erysimi), Painted Bug, Sawfly, Leaf Miner
commonDiseases: White Rust (Albugo candida), Alternaria Leaf Blight, Downy Mildew, Sclerotinia Stem Rot
preventionPractices: Sow before Oct 20 to escape peak aphid infestation; spray Dimethoate 30% EC or Thiamethoxam 25% WG if aphids exceed 20-25 aphids/plant; treat seed with Apron 35SD @ 6g/kg.
postHarvest: Harvest when 75% siliquae turn golden-yellow; thresh in morning to prevent pod shattering.
storageGuidance: Dry seeds to 8% moisture before bagging; store in moisture-proof gunny bags lined with polythene.
marketConsiderations: High demand in domestic edible oil extraction mills; MSP support active; premium price for higher oil content (>40%).
intercropping: Intercropped with Wheat (1:9 ratio), Chickpea (1:4 ratio), Barley.
riskFactors: Cloudy weather and high humidity promote severe aphid infestation and white rust; frost during flowering.
tips: Use certified varieties: Giriraj (DRMRIJ-31), RH-749, Pusa Mustard 25, NRCHB-101. Apply Single Super Phosphate (SSP) instead of DAP to supply essential Sulphur.

name: Paddy / Rice (धान / நெல் / ਝੋਨਾ / వరి)
suitableRegions: Punjab, Haryana, West Bengal, UP, Bihar, AP, Telangana, Tamil Nadu, Odisha, Chhattisgarh
climate: Hot and humid monsoon climate with abundant sunshine and water.
soilTypes: Clayey, Alluvial, Clay Loam with high water retention capacity
waterDesc: Maintain 2-5 cm standing water during tillering and panicle initiation. Adopt Alternate Wetting & Drying (AWD) to conserve up to 30% water.
seedRatePerAcre: 8 – 10 kg / acre for transplanted, 15 kg for Direct Seeded Rice (DSR)

fertilizerPlan.nitrogen: 120-150 kg N / ha (1/3 basal, 1/3 tillering, 1/3 panicle initiation)
fertilizerPlan.potash: 40 kg K2O / ha (half basal, half panicle stage)
fertilizerPlan.zinc: 25 kg Zinc Sulphate / ha basal to prevent Khaira disease

nutrientDeficiencies: Khaira disease / brown rusty pigmentation on young leaves (Zinc deficiency), yellowing of whole plant (Nitrogen).
commonPests: Brown Planthopper (BPH), Stem Borer, Leaf Folder, Gall Midge, Rice Hispa
commonDiseases: Bacterial Leaf Blight (BLB), Blast (Magnaporthe oryzae), Sheath Blight, False Smut
preventionPractices: Dip seedling roots in Chlorpyrifos solution; apply Tricyclazole 75% WP @ 0.6g/L for blast prevention; avoid stagnant deep flooding.
postHarvest: Harvest when 80-85% grains straw-colored; dry paddy to 14% moisture before milling.
storageGuidance: Store in clean, moisture-free godowns / CAP storage elevated on wooden pallets.
marketConsiderations: Large government MSP procurement operations via FCI; high export demand for Basmati varieties.
intercropping: Generally grown as sole crop; Azolla biofertilizer inter-cultivation in flooded fields.
riskFactors: Groundwater depletion under flood irrigation; lodging during late October rains; blast disease in humid spells.
tips: Adopt short-duration varieties like PR-126 (123 days) to save 20-25% water and allow timely wheat sowing without residue burning.

name: Chickpea / Desi Chana (चना / கொண்டைக்கடலை / ਛੋਲੇ / శనਗలు)
suitableRegions: Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Karnataka, UP, Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh
climate: Mild cool and dry climate during vegetative stage; warm sunny weather at maturity.
rainfall: 40 to 60 cm (Thrives under residual soil moisture)
soilTypes: Loamy, Black Clay Soil, Sandy Loam (well-drained, free of salinity)
waterDesc: 1-2 life-saving irrigations: 1st at branching (45 DAS), 2nd at pod filling (75 DAS). Highly sensitive to excess moisture/waterlogging.
spacing: 30 cm row-to-row, 10 cm plant-to-plant; Depth: 6-8 cm

fertilizerPlan.nitrogen: 20 kg N / ha (starter dose only; fixes atmospheric N via nodules)
fertilizerPlan.phosphorus: 40-50 kg P2O5 / ha (promotes strong root nodulation)
fertilizerPlan.biofertilizer: Treat seed with Rhizobium culture + PSB (Phosphate Solubilizing Bacteria)

nutrientDeficiencies: Pale green foliage (Nitrogen in nodule failure), stunted purple stems (Phosphorus).
commonPests: Gram Pod Borer (Helicoverpa armigera), Cutworm, Semilooper
commonDiseases: Fusarium Wilt, Ascochyta Blight, Collar Rot, Dry Root Rot
preventionPractices: Install 5 pheromone traps / acre for pod borer; spray NPV (Nuclear Polyhedrosis Virus) or Emamectin Benzoate 5% SG @ 0.5g/L at early larval instar; seed treatment with Trichoderma viride @ 5g/kg.
postHarvest: Sun-dry harvested plants for 3-4 days; thresh and clean; winnow to remove broken grains.
storageGuidance: Dry to 9% moisture; mix with neem oil (5 ml/kg) to prevent Pulse Beetle (Callosobruchus chinensis) infestation.
marketConsiderations: High domestic consumption for dal and besan; robust APMC demand with MSP safety net.
intercropping: Intercropped with Mustard (4:1 ratio), Barley, Linseed.
riskFactors: Excess rain or irrigation during flowering causes flower drop and vegetative overgrowth; Fusarium wilt in warm soils.
tips: Adds 30-40 kg atmospheric Nitrogen/ha to the soil, significantly reducing fertilizer costs for the succeeding crop. Recommended varieties: JG-11, GNG-1581, RVG-202, Pusa 372.

name: Cotton (कपास / பருத்தி / ਕਪਾਹ / పత్తి)
suitableRegions: Gujarat, Maharashtra, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan, Karnataka
climate: Warm and tropical with at least 180-200 frost-free days and bright sunshine during boll maturation.
rainfall: 60 to 100 cm uniformly distributed during growth
soilTypes: Deep Black Soil (Regur), Deep Alluvial Loam with good drainage
waterDesc: 4-6 irrigations at critical stages: Squaring (45 DAS), Flowering (70 DAS), Boll development (90-110 DAS). Drip irrigation highly recommended.
sowingWindow: 15 Apr – 20 May (North India), Jun – Jul (Central & South India)
seedRatePerAcre: 1.5 – 2.0 kg / acre (Bt Hybrid Cotton: 2 packets of 450g each)

fertilizerPlan.potash: 60 kg K2O / ha (split into basal + flowering)
fertilizerPlan.magnesium: Foliar spray of 1% Magnesium Sulphate + 1% 19:19:19 to prevent leaf reddening

nutrientDeficiencies: Leaf reddening and curling (Magnesium / Potassium deficiency), flower and boll shedding (Boron deficiency).
commonPests: Pink Bollworm (Pectinophora gossypiella), Whitefly, Thrips, Jassids, Aphids
commonDiseases: Cotton Leaf Curl Virus (CLCuV), Bacterial Blight, Root Rot, Alternaria Leaf Spot
preventionPractices: Install 5-8 pheromone traps / acre for Pink Bollworm; spray Diafenthiuron 50% WP @ 1g/L for whitefly; avoid late ratoon crop to break pest cycle.
postHarvest: Pick clean seed cotton in dry morning after dew evaporates; keep free of trash, dry leaves and moisture.
storageGuidance: Store in clean, dry, well-ventilated godowns protected from moisture and fire hazards.
marketConsiderations: High demand in ginning and textile spinning mills; CCI (Cotton Corporation of India) MSP procurement active.
intercropping: Intercropped with Green Gram (Moong), Black Gram (Urad), Cowpea, Soybean (1:2 ratio).
riskFactors: Pink bollworm resistance in Bt cotton; Whitefly transmitting leaf curl virus; unseasonal late October rains staining open bolls.
tips: Drip irrigation with fertigation increases yield by 25-30% while reducing water consumption by 45%. Recommended hybrids: RCH-659, US-51, Supercot.

name: Maize / Makka (मक्का / மக்காச்சோளம் / ਮੱਕੀ / మొక్కజొన్న)
suitableRegions: Karnataka, MP, Bihar, Maharashtra, Rajasthan, UP, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Punjab
climate: Warm temperate to tropical climate with ample sunlight.
soilTypes: Alluvial, Sandy Loam, Well-Drained Deep Loam rich in organic matter
waterDesc: 3-4 irrigations at critical stages: Knee-high (25-30 DAS), Tasseling (45-50 DAS), Silking (55-60 DAS), Grain dough stage (75-80 DAS).
sowingWindow: 15 Jun – 10 Jul (Kharif), Oct – Nov (Rabi), Feb – Mar (Spring Zaid)
spacing: 60 cm row-to-row, 20 cm plant-to-plant; Sowing depth: 4-5 cm

fertilizerPlan.nitrogen: 120 kg N / ha (1/3 basal, 1/3 knee-high, 1/3 tasseling stage)
fertilizerPlan.zinc: 25 kg Zinc Sulphate / ha once in two seasons

nutrientDeficiencies: White bud symptom in young leaves (Zinc deficiency), V-shaped yellowing on older leaves (Nitrogen).
commonPests: Fall Armyworm (Spodoptera frugiperda), Stem Borer (Chilo partellus), Shoot Fly
commonDiseases: Turcicum Leaf Blight, Maydis Leaf Blight, Banded Leaf and Sheath Blight, Charcoal Rot
preventionPractices: Apply whorl application of Emamectin Benzoate 5% SG @ 0.4g/L or Spinetoram 11.7% SC for Fall Armyworm at 15-20 DAS; treat seeds with Cyantraniliprole 19.8% + Thiamethoxam 19.8% FS.
postHarvest: Harvest when husk leaves dry and black layer forms at grain base; de-husk and shell cobs; dry grain to 12% moisture.
storageGuidance: Store in dry aerated bags; treat storage rooms against grain weevil and Angoumois grain moth.
marketConsiderations: High demand from poultry feed manufacturers, starch industries, and silage producers.
intercropping: Intercropped with Soybean, Cowpea, Green Gram (Moong) in 1:2 ratio.
riskFactors: Fall armyworm infestation in early vegetative whorl; waterlogging during early seedling stage.
tips: Dual-purpose crop generating high grain revenue and highly nutritious green fodder / silage for dairy cattle. High yielding hybrids: Pioneer 3396, DKC 9108, PMH-1.

name: Moong / Green Gram (मूंग / பாசிப்பயறு / ਮੂੰਗੀ / పెసలు)
suitableRegions: Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, UP, Punjab, Haryana, Gujarat, Bihar, Tamil Nadu
climate: Warm and dry climate; sensitive to waterlogging and frost.
soilTypes: Sandy Loam, Loamy, Alluvial (well-drained fertile soils)
waterDesc: 2-3 light irrigations: 1st at 20-25 DAS, 2nd at flowering (35 DAS), 3rd at pod filling (45-50 DAS). Stop irrigation 10 days before harvest.
spacing: 22.5 – 30 cm row-to-row, 10 cm plant-to-plant; Depth: 3-4 cm
nutrientDeficiencies: General chlorosis (Nitrogen if nodulation absent), purplish discoloration (Phosphorus).
commonPests: Whitefly (vector for YMV), Pod Borer, Thrips, Jassids
commonDiseases: Yellow Mosaic Virus (YMV), Cercospora Leaf Spot, Powdery Mildew, Macrophomina Blight
preventionPractices: Sow YMV-resistant varieties; spray Acetamiprid 20% SP @ 0.3g/L for whitefly control; seed treatment with Thiamethoxam 30% FS.
postHarvest: Pick mature pods in 2 pickings or harvest entire plant when 85% pods turn blackish brown.
storageGuidance: Dry seeds to 9% moisture; use Pusa bins with neem leaf layering to avoid bruchids.
marketConsiderations: High market price in retail pulses and sweet making; consistent APMC demand.
cropRotation: Ideal 60-day summer crop between Wheat harvest and Paddy transplanting (Wheat-Moong-Paddy).
riskFactors: Pre-monsoon rains during May harvesting cause pod sprouting and seed discolouration.
tips: Fills the 65-day gap between wheat harvest (April) and paddy transplanting (June). Adds 35-40 kg Nitrogen/ha into the soil. Recommended varieties: SML-668, IPM 205-7 (Virat), MH-421, Pusa Vishal.

name: Bajra / Pearl Millet (बाजरा / கம்பு / ਬਾਜਰਾ / సజ్జలు)
suitableRegions: Rajasthan, Maharashtra, Gujarat, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, MP, Tamil Nadu
climate: Hot and dry climate with high sunlight; extreme tolerance to high temperatures (>40°C).
rainfall: 30 to 50 cm (thrives in dryland rainfed farming)
soilTypes: Sandy Loam, Light Alluvial, Shallow Gravelly Soil
waterDesc: Thrives on monsoon rains; 1-2 life-saving irrigations during prolonged dry spells at boot and grain filling stages.
spacing: 45 cm row-to-row, 12-15 cm plant-to-plant; Depth: 2-3 cm

fertilizerPlan.nitrogen: 60-80 kg N / ha (half basal, half at 30 DAS)

nutrientDeficiencies: Stunted pale yellow plants (Nitrogen), reddish margins on leaf sheaths (Phosphorus).
commonPests: Shoot Fly, Stem Borer, Grasshopper, Earhead Midge
commonDiseases: Downy Mildew (Green Ear disease), Ergot, Rust, Smut
preventionPractices: Seed treatment with Metalaxyl 35 SD @ 6g/kg for Downy Mildew; soak seed in 10% salt water to remove light ergot sclerotia; rogue infected plants.
postHarvest: Harvest when earheads turn brown and grains harden; dry earheads in sun for a week before threshing.
storageGuidance: Dry threshed grain to 10-12% moisture; store in dry clay or metal silos.
marketConsiderations: Boosted by National Year of Millets (Shree Anna) initiative; growing industrial and healthy flour demand; high dry stover value for cattle.
intercropping: Intercropped with Cowpea, Moth Bean, Green Gram in 1:2 ratio.
riskFactors: Heavy rains and high humidity during flowering cause ergot and downy mildew infection; bird damage at milk stage.
tips: Rich in Iron, Zinc, and dietary fibre. Highly nutritious cattle dry fodder (kadbi). Recommended hybrids: HHB-67 Improved (65 days), MPMH-17, RHB-177, Proagro 9444.
